items.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: I really hadn’t thought about this in a long time to be honest with you... especially with Hank, all the things we’ve done, Mancini you know.

ctx.x: I started counting the albums you’ve been on and I lost track at 1,335.
I don’t have, oddly enough I don’t even have the old “Peter Gunn” things with Hank Mancini. That was twenty, forty, thirty years ago, something like that.
It’s just an amazing list, and along with the albums the people that you’ve been involved with musically. It’s quite impressive.

items.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: he did it for Hank... why not do something like “Shorty Rogers at Mom’s Place.” And Hank said no, it’s my music, I want to do it, if you want my music.

ctx.x: Yeah. And of course Ray Anthony could do what he wanted, he had a contract with Capitol, but I mean he did it for Hank and of course you know the rest. And Hank only had the album out on RCA Victor, but not the single. There were things like indescript things like “Mom’s Place” where there’s an off-the-road type cafe and bar where Peter Gunn used to hang out. And they were thinking how about Shorty Rogers, he’s with RCA Victor and he has a contract there, and why not do something like “Shorty Rogers at Mom’s…
And that was it, the rest is history. He was a wonderful orchestrator and a composer Hank is, or was.
